summary: Granular model-lock mismatch observed during tenant shadowing leading to cross-cohort fallback
description:
Issue summary:
During a shadowing experiment for customer LexiHealth's route, a subset of requests that should have been bound to the shadow cohort's model-lock were routed to the primary variant, causing unexpected fallback responses and content mismatch for affected sessions.

Impact:
- ~2.3% of transactions for the tenant saw mixed-model outputs over a 27-minute window (03:12–03:39 UTC).
- Customer reported quality regressions for a production subset (billing unaffected but UX degraded).

Environment:
- Production (us-east)
- Tenant: lexi-001 (enterprise)
- Rolling canary: traffic mirror of 5% to shadow variant (rw-instruct-1.0 -> open-llama-13B-v2 shadow)

Steps to reproduce (customer & internal):
1) Enable 5% traffic mirror for route /chat for tenant lexi-001 with shadow variant pinned to open-llama-13B-v2.
2) Send bursts of conversational requests with persistent session cookies to simulate real traffic.
3) Observe routing decisions in route logs and compare model_id vs model_lock headers.

Observed behavior:
- Some sessions show header model_lock: open-llama-13B-v2 on the control plane, but the downstream serving runtime selected rw-instruct-1.0 for the actual inference call.
- Fallbacks to primary variant occurred without corresponding health-probe or capacity events.
- Edge traces show an intermittent mismatch between the epoch snapshot used by edge routing and the model-lock table in the orchestrator during mirror commit windows.

Expected behavior:
- Shadowed requests should be mirrored to the shadow variant while the primary continues serving the production model. Model-lock must remain coherent across the control-plane snapshot used by edge and the local route memoization.

Relevant logs/traces:
- Orchestrator trace: https://logs.redwood.ai/trace/9b3f7c (samples showing commit_id mismatch).
- Edge routing traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/edge/lexi-001/2026-03-13-03 (filtered).
- Serving runtime debug snippet (excerpt):
  "selected_model": "rw-instruct-1.0", "requested_lock": "open-llama-13B-v2", "route_epoch": 4521, "lock_epoch": 4520

Notes:
- No GPU preemption or autoscaler events recorded during window.
- No rate-limit or 5xx spikes correlated in monitoring dashboards.
comments: 2026-03-13 03:45 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer reported inconsistent responses. Confirmed 2.3% error rate in quick analytics check. Escalated to SRE and assigned to Luca.

2026-03-13 04:05 UTC - SRE (Luca): Initial hypothesis: snapshot skew between control-plane snapshot writer and edge snapshot consumer during mirror commit. Putting rollout on hold and enabling routing override for lexi-001 (force shadow mirror to explicit split).

2026-03-13 05:20 UTC - SRE (Luca): Applied temporary control-plane override: set explicit route binding for tenant lexi-001 to bypass edge memoization. Observed immediate drop in mixed outputs. Case remains open to investigate root cause.
2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - Customer (LexiHealth - Emma R): Appreciates quick mitigation; requests confirmation before resuming mirror. Would like timeline and postmortem once RCA done.
2026-03-14 11:30 UTC - Product (Diego): Noted similar behavior historically during ‘commit-window shrink’ tests. Suggested checking epoch advance and snapshot commit ordering in orchestrator v2.1.
investigation_notes: Checked orchestrator commit logs for epoch range 4518-4523: observed one delayed write at 03:12:03 UTC that replayed at 03:12:40 UTC. Edge snapshot consumer had a 30s poll interval configured -> potential race.
Correlated route_epoch vs lock_epoch mismatch in serving runtime logs. Several requests show route_epoch > lock_epoch by 1 which allowed memoized binding to fall back to primary model path.

Reproduced locally with synthetic driver by simulating delayed snapshot commit and edge poll offset; confirmed memoization used stale route metadata resulting in mixed-model selection for sessions that resumed mid-commit.

Preliminary hypothesis: under small mirror percentages, the combination of edge memoization TTL + non-atomic commit window for model-lock updates allowed a transient window where requests read partial state (route updated but lock table not yet applied).

Checked related PRs: referenced PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1987 which changed commit batching; opened follow-up ticket INT-431 for an orchestrator patch to make commit application atomic for route+lock updates.
Dashboards: routing-coherence-alerts spike aligns with commit replay times. No serving resource pressure detected.
resolution_summary: Mitigation applied: paused mirror rollout for lexi-001 and applied routing override to force explicit split so shadow traffic is handled deterministically. Investigations point to a commit ordering/race in orchestrator snapshot writer vs edge poll cadence. Workplan: implement atomic commit in orchestrator (INT-431), increase edge poll frequency temporarily, and add a short guard that rejects mixed-epoch requests at edge. Pending: code change and controlled re-rollout after tests.
next_steps: INT-431: implement and test atomic route+lock commit in orchestrator (assigned to infra team)
Adjust edge snapshot poll interval for us-east to 10s while patch is developed
Run a deterministic canary (10% internal traffic) for 2 hours with added auditing to confirm zero mixed-model responses
Produce postmortem doc and communicate ETA to LexiHealth (target: 2026-03-18)
Add routing-coherence monitor and an automated alert that triggers when route_epoch != lock_epoch for in-flight requests
